cards.explanation: The answer is False. On the Sabbath, God says, “You must not do any work; wherever you live, it is a Sabbath to the LORD.” Whether the house is in the middle of the camp or off at the edge, it's the same rest. Not even one little email from the kitchen table, friends.

The answer is unleavened bread. God says, “For seven days you must eat unleavened bread.” Seven days, friends. As a cookie guy, I have questions about a week of that, but I just follow the instructions.

The answer is True, friends. On the first day, “…you are to hold a sacred assembly; you are not to do any regular work.” The seventh day gets the same: “On the seventh day there shall be a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work.” So the feast has a sacred assembly at each end.

The answer is that he waves it, friends. God says, “And he shall wave the sheaf before the LORD so that it may be accepted on your behalf…” So the priest takes the very first of the harvest and lifts it up before the LORD for the people. The timing is set too: “the priest is to wave it on the day after the Sabbath.” If I tried waving a sheaf with this mustache, there'd be grain on my ceiling.

The answer is False. No bread, no roasted grain and no new grain “…until the very day you have brought this offering to your God.” And it isn't a one-time rule: “This is to be a permanent statute for the generations to come, wherever you live.”

The answer is fifty. God says, “You shall count off fifty days until the day after the seventh Sabbath, and then present an offering of new grain to the LORD.” Seven full weeks is forty-nine days, and the day after makes fifty. The math checks out, even for a stamper.

The answer is baked with leaven. The two loaves are “…each made from two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour, baked with leaven, as the firstfruits to the LORD.” That's different from the unleavened bread earlier in the chapter. Different feast, different loaves.

The answer is for the generations to come. God says, “This is to be a permanent statute wherever you live for the generations to come.” No end date is given. It's a day for the children's children and the ones after them.

The answer is the poor and the foreign resident. God says, “Leave them for the poor and the foreign resident. I am the LORD your God.” Leaving the edges and the gleanings is the whole instruction. Even I'd have to leave the last chocolate chip on the tray, and that would be a hard day.

The answer is trumpet blasts. God says the first day of the seventh month is “…a day of rest, a sacred assembly announced by trumpet blasts.” No group chat needed, just trumpets. Everybody within earshot gets the message, friends.

The answer is to humble themselves. God says, “You shall hold a sacred assembly and humble yourselves, and present a food offering to the LORD.” It comes right alongside the assembly and the offering. This day is a different mood than a party, friends.

The answer is False. God says, “You are not to do any work at all.” and He calls it “…a permanent statute for the generations to come, wherever you live.” The whole day is rest, assembly or no assembly. Not even a little catch-up, friends.

The answer is the evening of the ninth day. God says, “From the evening of the ninth day of the month until the following evening you are to keep your Sabbath.” So the rest starts the night before the tenth day. That's evening to evening.

The answer is True, friends. The seven days finish, and then God adds one more: “On the eighth day you are to hold a sacred assembly and present a food offering to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly; you must not do any regular work.” Just when you think the feast is wrapping up, there's one more day. It's like finding one last cookie at the bottom of the box.

The answer is fruit and branches from trees. God says, “On the first day you are to gather the fruit of majestic trees, the branches of palm trees, and the boughs of leafy trees and of willows of the brook.” That's quite a shopping list for one day, friends. Palm branches, leafy boughs and willows, all in one pile.

The answer is rejoice. God says, “And you are to rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.” That's a different tone from the Day of Atonement, where the word was “humble yourselves.” A whole week of it, friends.

The answer is so later generations know God had Israel live in booths, friends. God says it's “…so that your descendants may know that I made the Israelites dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt.” It's a yearly way for their descendants to know it. And He signs it: “I am the LORD your God.”

The answer is False, friends. The last verse says, “So Moses announced to the Israelites the appointed feasts of the LORD.” God had told him to “Speak to the Israelites…” and the chapter ends with Moses announcing the feasts to them. This calendar was not a priests-only memo.
